sentence: These four verbs are also among the handful that carry an irregular subjunctive stem, a different irregularity covered in full in [the French subjunctive breakdown](/french-subjunctive/), where avoir and être turn out to be the only two verbs in the language that also swap their subjunctive endings, not just their stem. Être also sits behind a separate irregularity pattern with nothing to do with its own conjugation: it\'s the auxiliary [French reflexive verbs](/french-reflexive-verbs/) always take instead of avoir, where the real complication isn\'t the auxiliary choice but when the past participle agrees with the subject and when it doesn\'t.

target_quote: answer: 'Yes, without exception, across all four types Larousse identifies. Per the OQLF, être is mandatory the moment a pronominal verb hits a compound tense, no matter which of the four categories it falls into. That holds whether it has a subjective pronominal sense (je me suis réjoui), réciproque (ils se seraient mariés), one with no non-reflexive form at all (ils se seront évanouis), or sens passif. Ordinary French verbs mostly default to avoir, with être kept for a short list of movement and existence verbs, but being pronominal at all overrides that default, regardless of what the verb would otherwise take.',
